overview.mechanism: Combines metformin-mediated glucose regulation with inhibition of incretin degradation by teneligliptin.
uses: Glycemic control in type 2 diabetes; exact fixed-dose formulation and release characteristics matter.

paragraphs.text: A placebo-controlled trial found improved HbA1c when teneligliptin was added to metformin over 24 weeks. This supports add-on efficacy, not interchangeability of every fixed-dose product.
A fixed-dose bioequivalence study involved healthy volunteers and compared specific modified-release formulations. It does not establish safety of the combination in advanced CKD or dialysis.
The metformin component remains limiting: the US metformin label contraindicates use below eGFR 30 mL/min/1.73 m². Single-agent teneligliptin renal data do not remove this restriction.

sources.citation: Ji et al. Efficacy and safety of teneligliptin added to metformin in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomized placebo-controlled study. Endocrinol Diabetes Metab. 2021;4:e00222. PubMed PMID: 33855222.
Pharmacokinetics of a Fixed-Dose Combination of Teneligliptin Hydrochloride Hydrate and Modified-Release Metformin Under Fasting and Fed Conditions in Healthy Subjects. PubMed PMID: 36597442.
